decisions.evidence: The parenthetical lem-of-naturals-positive proves positivity and natural arithmetic, not identification of an integer quotient with real division. The preceding declared embedding chain preserves multiplication: q=dk implies E(q)=E(d)E(k), hence E(k)=E(q)/E(d) since d>=1. Thus the mathematics is sound by an elementary derivation but the exact citation is inaccurate. Published source retained; owner strategy: cite the embedding chain already declared and show this identity.

The sentence d divides q(x), so q(x)/d is a natural >=1 omits the sign/identification argument. Write q(x)=dk with k integer; q(x)>0 and d>0 imply k>0, and lem-nat-embeds-int identifies k with a unique nonzero natural. This is elementary nonfatal polish; p(x)=0 and negative numerators cause no exception. The least-denominator proof and coprime converse are otherwise sound, including q(0)=1. Published source retained; owner strategy: insert this short derivation.

The asserted singleton indicator is sound but has no supplied approximation. On [0,1], phi_n(x)=max(0,1-n|x-a|) is continuous, equals 1 at a, and is eventually 0 at each x != a; arbitrarily close points different from a prove discontinuity, including a=0,1. This is nonfatal omitted elementary verification. Published source retained; owner editorial strategy: add this witness and limit/discontinuity check.
